title: Copying a record to the table
statement: For every $m\in\mathbb{N}$, there are a finite state set $P$, a two-work-tape machine $R$, entry and exit states, and a constant $C\in\mathbb{N}$ such that the following holds. Given a header word $h$, a list $es$ of lists of words, and a list $e$ of words of length $m$, assume every field in the table formed from $h$ and the flattened $es$ is nonempty. If a configuration starts in the entry state, tape 0 has its head at $o$ and stores the table encoding with blank cells from its end onward, and tape 1 stores the joined encoding of $e$ at its head, then there is a time $t\le C(L+E+1)$, where $L$ and $E$ are the lengths of the table and record encodings, at which the machine is in the exit state and tape 0 has appended the encoding of $e$ at the offset following all table fields. No earlier time below $t$ reaches the exit state, and up to time $t$ both heads remain within distance $C(L+E+1)$ of their initial positions; the final tape contents elsewhere, as well as the other configuration data, are unchanged.
